note: Reads 4 bytes from the external socket fuzzer into a stack buffer; the received bytes are attacker-controlled input for the daemon path.
The 4-byte command is interpreted to decide whether the daemon continues, crashes, or exits.

The safety obligation is that the command buffer must contain a complete, valid 4-byte token before it is compared; otherwise the daemon can mis-handle the control path and continue with invalid state.
On the crash path, the daemon uses the current target pid to terminate the target process.
The target process is force-killed after the control token is processed; this is the observable sink reached from the socket input path.
